[00:00] Samir: alright hey everyone thanks for joining on time um this is Samir from Redwood, with me is Elena our SE and Javier from CS. happy to run through renewal thoughts and the regional bump.
[00:14] Caroline: thanks Samir, appreciate it. quick context — we've been ramping prod since Q4, usage peaked the last two weeks, and we want to lock in capacity and add eu-west for data residency for some EU clients.
[00:25] Marcus: yes the p95 latency on long prompt flows is creeping up during peak windows, we're seeing some tail lat spikes, so we want to understand dedicated pool options and fallback behaviors.
[00:38] Elena: ok great, so two parallel asks — (1) capacity uplift committed vs burst and (2) region activation eu-west — both are doable but there are tradeoffs. committed nodes give stable p95, burst is cheaper historically but can have cold-start like effects if not warmed.
[00:54] Caroline: and we have compliance constraints — data that must stay in eu for a subset of customers, also Priya here will want to review encryption/KMS details.
[01:05] Priya: hi — yes SOC2 is in flight, we need the audit contact and if there's any change to retention or access logs once we move traffic to the new region.
[01:14] Samir: totally; we have an enterprise security packet that covers SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, KMS integrations. we'll surface the specific KMS flows for private deployments.
[01:23] Ethan: quick infra Q — for the eu region, what's the expected cold-start window if we spin up a dedicated pool vs using hosted region with routing?
[01:33] Elena: good question. dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) is instant for hot models, for new containers first init may be a minute but tokens stream fine. hosted cross-region routing can add ~30–150ms of network latency depending on peering. also KV cache warm-up matters — if you have long-running sessions cache keeps p50 low.
[01:48] Marcus: when you say 30–150ms that's bench from Redwood's tests or internal nets? we're sensitive to the p95 under 350ms target.
[01:58] Elena: our tests are from standard cloud regions, but we can run the same benchmark with your routes — that's actually one of the next steps: Elena will run a 24 hour benchmark using your sample traffic to measure p50/p95 and cost units on dedicated flavors.
[02:12] Marcus: ok that helps. on cost, we are looking at committed + 15% burst. do you have a quick sense of pricing delta between dedicated1 (standard quant) and dedicated2 (int8 quant) models?
[02:26] Samir: short answer: quantized models (int8) can be 30–40% cheaper per token but we need to validate quality on your prompts. Elena will pair the perf runs with quality checks. Also we can show price for dedicated vs hosted for the uplift chunk.
[02:40] Caroline: timeline wise, our procurement window closes end of March, we'd like signed amendments by March 10 to allow provisioning.
[02:50] Samir: that's doable. we'll target sending the amendment by Fri 2/25 and ask for a week review.
[02:57] Priya: on the private/VPC option — part of our risk team prefers customer-managed routing and key management. can Redwood support HSM/KMS with BYOK?
[03:08] Elena: yes, Private deployments support customer KMS integration (BYOK) and optional HSM via partner. there's some ops setup but it's standard in our Private offering. I'll attach the KMS flow doc; small caveat is audit logs retention defaults differ by plan but we can mirror your retention with an add-on.
[03:27] Priya: ok can you include the retention numbers and attestations, and the SOC2 auditor contact?
[03:33] Samir: yes Priya, we'll include that in the security packet — Javier will put the auditor contact info and retention table in the follow-up.
[03:40] Javier: noted, will attach.
[03:43] [05:02] (brief side noise)
[05:16] Marcus: also curious about fallback behavior — if dedicated pool saturates, do you automatically route to hosted fallback and is that cross-region? we want predictable degradation not blackouts.
[05:29] Elena: we have smart routing and fallback policies. you can configure route by cost or latency and specify automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. if you want, we can set region fallback rules so eu traffic falls back within eu first, then to us-west if needed.
[05:45] Marcus: great, that aligns with our SRE playbooks.
[05:51] Caroline: one more thing — we're planning a short pilot for onprem (airgapped) for one regulated client in Q3. what's a realistic path?
[06:02] Elena: onprem is a longer runway — typically a couple months to package and validate, but we do offer an initial private pilot in a VPC first to validate controls then an onprem airgap transition. we can scope a phased plan in the SOW.
[06:15] Caroline: ok phased sounds right.
[06:18] [07:50] Samir: quick commercial note — renewal structure we usually do a 12 month commitment with an uplift tiered discount — we'll propose a base + eu-west add-on + burst pool. Any constraints on payment terms?
[07:43] Priya: procurement prefers net45 for the finance team but we can be flexible if there's a discount trade.
[07:51] Samir: we'll include net45 in the amendment; discount tiers shown if commit >= 20% uplift.
[08:00] Marcus: regarding telemetry — does Redwood expose token-level cost traces per API key? we need to map spend to product lines.
[08:10] Elena: yes console has token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards; you can also export traces to your datalake. small note: export retention by default is 90 days unless you purchase longer retention.
[08:22] Ethan: would love a CSV export for internal chargeback.
[08:26] Javier: we can include a sample export format.
[08:29] [10:00] Caroline: let's talk numbers quickly — rough ask is +20% committed capacity, enable eu-west as a paid add-on, and a burst pool for seasonal spikes. can you do all that within a single amendment?
[10:12] Samir: yes single amendment with line items: committed tokens (or gpu units), eu region flat fee, burst commit. price will show monthly equivalent and a committed discount.
[10:22] Caroline: one more logistical — who owns the rollout playbook and timing for cutover? we need an ops lead from Redwood for the activation weekend.
[10:32] Elena: Elena (SE) will own the activation playbook and we typically include a runbook and a post-cutover run to validate KV cache and latency. Javier will be CSM on follow-up.
[10:42] Caroline: perfect.

[14:02] Elena: yes we'll simulate your session shape, test with warm KV cache scenarios, measure p50/p95 and requests/sec. include perf + quality thresholds so we can measure any degradation with quantized models.
[14:15] Marcus: and can you run it on both dedicated1 (fp16) and dedicated2 (int8) so we can compare cost/latency/quality?
[14:24] Elena: absolutely. that's in the benchmark scope.
[14:28] Caroline: any blocker for us to sign the amendment soon?

[18:45] Marcus: good to know, we'll include the eval set.

[25:34] Elena: cache persistence is per-instance and we have sticky sessions for hot keys; across restarts there's a rebuild time, but we can do pre-warm strategies like keepalive traffic and background cache priming.
